title: 1985 AHSME Problem 12
statement: Let \(p,\) \(q\) and \(r\) be distinct prime numbers, where \(1\) is not considered a prime. Which of the following is the smallest positive perfect cube having \(n=pq^2r^4\) as a divisor?

solutions.text: A perfect cube has prime exponents divisible by \(3.\) The least multiples of \(3\) that are at least \(1,\) \(2,\) and \(4\) are \(3,\) \(3,\) and \(6,\) respectively. Thus the smallest possible cube is \[ p^3q^3r^6=(pqr^2)^3. \] Therefore the correct answer is D.
hints: Every prime exponent in a perfect cube is a multiple of \(3\)
Raise the exponents \(1,\) \(2,\) and \(4\) to the least larger multiples of \(3\)
